topIssues.title: linter/bigint: suggested fix emits an unbound qualifier when op-service/bigs is aliased or dot-imported
topIssues.author: kyle4814
topIssues.body:
### Summary

The `bigint` custom linter's suggested fix decides two things separately that
have to agree:

- **whether** to add the `op-service/bigs` import — `fileHasImport()` matches on the import **path**
- **what identifier** to qualify the rewritten call with — `buildStrictCall()` hardcodes `"bigs."`

When a file already imports `op-service/bigs` under any name other than `bigs`,
the import edit is suppressed (path matches) *and* the emitted call references
an identifier that isn't bound. `golangci-lint --fix` then rewrites the file
into code that doesn't compile.

Observed on `develop` at `2258ea57`.

### Reproduction

Add a testdata package containing a file that imports the package under an
alias, then run the analyzer with suggested fixes applied:

```go
package a

import (
	"math/big"

	mybigs "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/bigs"
)

var _ = mybigs.Uint64Strict

func aliased() {
	x := new(big.Int)
	_ = x.Uint64()
}
```

`analysistest.RunWithSuggestedFixes` produces:

```go
import (
	"math/big"

	mybigs "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/bigs"
)
...
	_ = bigs.Uint64Strict(x)   // undefined: bigs
```

The dot-import form (`. "…/bigs"`) fails the same way — the fix emits a
`bigs.` qualifier where the call should be unqualified. A blank import (`_`)
binds no identifier at all, so it also needs a usable import added.

### Why this isn't currently caught

`linter/analyzers/bigint/bigint_test.go` uses `analysistest.Run`, which checks
diagnostics only and never applies the suggested fixes. The whole fix path —
`buildStrictCall`, `fileHasImport`, `importEdit`, and the one-shot
`addImportEdit` logic — has no test coverage today.

### Impact

Latent, not currently triggered. Across `develop` at `2258ea57` I count 188
plain imports of `op-service/bigs`, zero named aliases, zero dot imports, and
one blank import (`op-service/testutils/depguard/depguard_test.go`) which
contains no `.Uint64()` calls. So no file in the tree today would be broken by
`--fix`; the defect would surface the first time someone aliases that import in
a file containing a flagged call.

### Suggested direction

Resolve the package's actual local binding in the file and use it for both
decisions, rather than deciding the import and the qualifier independently:
alias → use the alias; dot import → unqualified call; blank import → treat as
absent so a usable import is added.

I have a patch along those lines plus `RunWithSuggestedFixes` golden tests
covering the plain, aliased and dot-import forms, if that would be useful — happy
to open a PR.

topPRs.title: devfeatures: remove SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION dev feature flag
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #21689, which made the flag default-on via a short-circuit in the `isDevFeatureEnabled` predicates. With both predicates hardcoded true, every branch on the flag is a constant, so this PR removes the flag entirely:

- Remove the `SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION` / `SuperRootGamesMigrationFlag` constants and the short-circuits from `DevFeatures.sol` and `op-core/devfeatures`, restoring the plain bitwise-AND predicate on both sides. The retired bit value is documented in the `DevFeatures.sol` natspec so it isn't accidentally reused.
- Flatten every conditional to the enabled side: `OPContractsManagerV2` (`_isPermittedInstruction`, `_assertValidFullConfig`), `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` (`isSuperMode` now always derived from the ASR's respected game type), `Deploy.s.sol` (drops the now-unreachable `getDeployInputV2`), `DeployImplementations.s.sol`, `DeployOPChain.s.sol` (drops `isSuperRoot` state + helper), `VerifyOPCM.s.sol`, `ForkL1Live.s.sol`.
- Remove the test-only env plumbing (`Config.devFeatureSuperRootGamesMigration()`, `FeatureFlags.sol` wiring) and the `WithDevFeatureEnabled` calls in op-devstack / op-acceptance-tests.
- Delete tests that were permanently skipped under the default-on flag (incl. the legacy standard-mode `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator_TestInit` hierarchy). The ZK gating tests (`ZKDG-NOSHAPE` / feature-enabled-no-impl) from that hierarchy are ported onto the surviving super-mode fixture since that validator branch is live in super mode.
- Semver bumps for the three contracts whose bytecode changes vs the base branch: `OPContractsManagerV2` 7.2.3, `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` 2.12.1, `L2DevFeatureFlags` 1.3.1. semver-lock and the NUT bundle regenerated accordingly (bundle deltas: L2DevFeatureFlags initcode, L2ContractsManager constructor arg, upgradePredeploys target address).
- Update `docs/ai/devfeatures.md`.

Closes #21662.

## Test plan

- `just pr` in `packages/contracts-bedrock`: all checks pass. (Locally, `semver-diff` can't resolve a merge base against `develop` in a shallow clone; verified manually that all three changed semver-lock entries carry version bumps vs this PR's base branch.)
- Full `just test-dev`: 2233 passed, 0 failed, 141 skipped.
- `go test ./op-core/devfeatures/...` passes; `go build` on op-devstack/sysgo and the touched op-acceptance-tests packages; gofmt/vet clean.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: clarify feature release lifecycle
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
Clarifies the smart contract release process agreed during the July 21 Network Upgrades Weekly:

- Require development feature flags to be removed on `develop` before audit, while production-supported `SystemConfig` system features may remain configurable.
- Audit the release candidate's exact commit, reuse it for the final tag when no fixes are required, and create proposal branches lazily.
- Make contract verification failures release blockers and remove the unconditional assumption that `op-deployer` releases from a proposal branch.
- Fix the versioning policy's release-process links.

Validation:

- `git diff --check`
- `mdbook build packages/contracts-bedrock/book` (passes with the existing `mdbook-mermaid` version warning)

topPRs.title: docs: add SolidRPC to RPC directory
topPRs.author: DamianFigiel
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds SolidRPC to the OP Stack production RPC provider directory.

The listing includes the OP Stack networks currently supported by SolidRPC:

- Mainnets: OP Mainnet, Base, Ink, Unichain, World Chain, Lisk, and Zora
- Testnets: OP Sepolia, Base Sepolia, Lisk Sepolia, Unichain Sepolia, and Zora Sepolia

**Tests**

Documentation-only change.

- Verified the listed networks against the current SolidRPC network catalog
- Ran `git diff --check`

**Additional context**

- Website: https://solidrpc.io
- Documentation: https://solidrpc.io/docs
- Supported networks: https://solidrpc.io/docs/networks
- Pricing: https://solidrpc.io/docs/pricing

SolidRPC provides authenticated EVM JSON-RPC endpoints over HTTPS with full and archive access where available.

**Metadata**

No related issue.
